messages.body_plain:
Ah, I figured it out.
Turns out there was also an older incompatible vesion of R (2.7.*) on
the cluster. I had to get rid of it so the Rhipe C engine could launch
the correct R version.

messages.body_plain:
Hi,
The only way I found to call Rhipe without permissions problems is
executing R as sudo.
Is this the way it should be? or am I doing something wrong?
Cheers,

messages.subject: Re: Is there a way to call Rhipe without executing R as sudo?
messages.subject_clean: Is there a way to call Rhipe without executing R as sudo?
messages.body_plain:
Yes there is!:)

I found it reading this post:
http://groups.google.com/group/rhipe/browse_thread/thread/51a316c67b3d0ad/0021593277b57be9?lnk=gst&q=root#0021593277b57be9

Just install hadoop with hadoop user as described in:
http://www.michael-noll.com/tutorials/running-hadoop-on-ubuntu-linux-single-node-cluster/

Install Rhipe and: sudo chown -R hadoop:hadoop /usr/local/lib/R

Well, here it stays the answer for the next one!

messages.body_plain:
You need the devel version of R. I.e built with shared library support.
The errors you get e.g.

 display.cc:96: error: ‘protect’ was not declared in this scope
> display.cc:111: error: ‘unprotect’ was not declared in this scope

are because of the lack of the devel version of R

Cheers
Saptarshi

> > > such file or directory
> > > ERROR: compilation failed for package 'Rhipe'
> > > ** Removing '/usr/local/lib/R/site-library/Rhipe'
>
> > > It looks like the g++ compiler can't resolve the macro, but I'm not
> > > sure as I'm definitely not a C++ guy. Can anybody suggest me what I'm
> > > missing?
>
> > > Thanks,
>
> > > Masa Nakamura (masayang)
messages.body_snippet:
I thought I solved the problem. It was caused by an old version of
R(2.7) that came with Amazon EMR.
I upgraded it to 2.11 and Rhipe is working nicely so far.

Thanks.

Masa Nakamura (masayang)

On Ju

Dear all,

I am trying to download the airline dataset using the example code
from RHIPE guide.
I have a cluster with CentOS, hadoop 2.0 and RHIPE.

It is not working and I do not have a clue why...
T

This is a tricky example to run. It depends on wget or curl being present.
And is not really what it's meant for. try some other examples before this.

I'd have to run it on my cluster to see why.

It might take time.

Saptarshi

messages.subject: Using Rhipe with RStudio Server
messages.subject_clean: Using Rhipe with RStudio Server
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am able use Rhipe correctly in R in the command line using my linux
server. It is able to use the HDFS. I've run tests, and they all work.

However, I am trying to use RStudio Server to connect to my R
environment, via remote connection. Has anywone used RStudio Server
with Rhipe? It seems to be working, RStudio Server anyways; I'm able
to login and use the R environment on my remote server. It's when I
load the library(Rhipe) on the client side, using RStudio's web-
interface, that I run into problems.

It pulls up the warning:

Warning messages:
1: In onload.2(libname, pkgname) :
  Rhipe requires the HADOOP or HADOOP_BIN environment variable to be
present
 $HADOOP/bin/hadoop or $HADOOP_BIN/hadoop should exists
2: In onload.2(libname, pkgname) :
  HADOOP_BIN is missing, using $HADOOP/bin

Afterwards, I type in rhinit(), and I get this:

/bin/hadoop jar /usr/local/lib/R/site-library/Rhipe/java/Rhipe.jar
org.godhuli.rhipe.PersonalServer localhost /tmp/RtmpWbI6Mj/
sockets32e81977 /tmp/RtmpWbI6Mj/signal1d0278a4 0
sh: /bin/hadoop: not found

Saying all this, I don't run into this problem using R directly on my
linux server, via command line. Rhipe works fine there, at least so
far running the tests.

Please let me know if anyone has had experience with RStudio Server,
or if there is any suggestions on other software to access Rhipe, via
a remote linux server.

I am using Ubuntu 10.10 (64bit), Apache Hadoop 0.20.2, RHIPE 0.65.4,
protobuf 2.3.0, R version 2.13.0, and Hive 0.7.1

Let me know if you need other information.

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I'm running through the Airline Dataset Example given in the RHIPE
documentation. I was hoping to at least get as far as a graphing
example. Before I go any farther, please forgive my lack of
programming skills if this seems kind of obvious or something.
Hopefully, it isn't a major issue.

Anyways, I've gotten down to section 3.4.1, which is trying to graph
the top 20 cities. Everything, for the most part, seems to be working
correctly, up to this far in section 3 (I skipped section 3.3).

This is what I've typed in so far in R (relating to section 3.4.1):

map <- expression({
  a <- do.call("rbind",map.values)
  inbound <- table(a[,'origin'])
  outbound <- table(a[,'dest'])
  total <- table(unlist(c(a[,'origin'],a['dest'])))
  for(n in names(total)){
    inb <- if(is.na <http://is.na>(inbound[n])) 0 else inbound[n]
    ob <- if(is.na <http://is.na>(outbound[n])) 0 else outbound[n]
    rhcollect(n, c(inb,ob, total[n]))
  }
})
reduce <- expression(
    pre={sums <- c(0,0,0)},
    reduce = {
      sums <- sums+apply(do.call("rbind",reduce.values),2,sum)
    },
    post = {
      rhcollect(reduce.key, sums)
    }
    )
mapred$rhipe_map_buff_size <- 15
z <-
rhmr(map=map,reduce=reduce,combiner=TRUE,inout=c("sequence","sequence")
          ,ifolder="/airline/blocks/",ofolder="/airline/volume"
          ,mapred=mapred)
rhex(z,async=TRUE)

counts <- rhread("/airline/volume")
aircode <- unlist(lapply(counts, "[[",1))
count <- do.call("rbind",lapply(counts,"[[",2))
results <- data.frame(aircode=aircode,
                      inb=count[,1],oub=count[,2],all=count[,3]
                      ,stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
results <- results[order(results$all,decreasing=TRUE),]

----

To this point, everything is working correctly (at least it appears
so). Then I try to execute this piece of code:

results$airport <- sapply(results$aircode,function(r){
nam <- ap[ap$iata==r,'airport']
if(length(nam)==0) r else nam
})

The error I get is this:

Error in FUN(c("ORD", "ATL", "DFW", "LAX", "PHX", "DEN", "DTW",
"IAH",  :
  object 'ap' not found

I've received this kind of error before (object '' not found) in
earlier pieces of section 3, and I was able to alleviate it by
changing the code a bit (I think it was some errors in the RHIPE user
guide given). However, here, I'm stuck. I'm not sure what to change/
add if anything. I'm hoping it's not something major. It doesn't seem
so.

Does anyone have any ideas? Again, if it seems simple, excuse my
ignorance. I'm just hoping to graph something, and I probably won't go
farther. I was hoping to demonstrate something graphically to my team.

Appreciate the help,

Jordan
